Posterior draws of pointwise log likelihoods

Source: R/log-lik.R
log_lik.Rd

Evaluate each fitting observation at draws from the coefficient posterior. This leaves the scalar stats::logLik() method supplied by mgcv unchanged.

Usage

log_lik(model, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gam'
log_lik(
  model,
  ...,
  n_draws = NULL,
  chains = NULL,
  diagnostics = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  method = c("gaussian", "mh", "user"),
  draws = NULL,
  unconditional = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'bam'
log_lik(
  model,
  ...,
  n_draws = NULL,
  chains = NULL,
  diagnostics = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  method = c("gaussian", "mh", "user"),
  draws = NULL,
  unconditional = FALSE
)

Arguments

model

A fitted independent-response gam or bam model.

...

Additional arguments to post_draws(), such as burnin, thin or mvn_method. Prediction at new observations and frequentist covariance matrices are not supported.

n_draws

Positive integer; total coefficient draws across chains. Defaults to 4000 when generating draws. Supplied draws determine their own count; an explicit count must agree.

chains

positive integer or NULL; number of chains. NULL uses one chain, or the chain mapping in supplied draws. n_draws must be divisible by chains. Burn-in is applied separately to each MH chain.

diagnostics

logical; calculate coefficient R-hat, effective sample sizes, and Monte Carlo standard errors using the optional posterior package.

seed

Optional random seed. The caller's random-number state is retained.

method

One of "gaussian", "mh" or "user"; see post_draws().

draws

A numeric matrix with one row per draw and one column per coefficient, in fitted coefficient order. Used with method = "user".

unconditional

Include the smoothing-parameter covariance correction when available, using mgcv::vcov.gam(). Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A numeric matrix with draws in rows and retained fitting observations in columns. Attribute observation gives their original fitting-row indices after any fitting subset; gratia describes the sampling assumptions. The sampling attribute retains chain identities and requested coefficient diagnostics; as_mcmc_draws() converts the likelihood matrix by chain. Impossible observations may have log likelihood -Inf; invalid numerical calculations produce an error. LOO and WAIC require finite log likelihoods.

Details

The result contains log densities or log probability masses, including their normalising constants and fitting weights. Smoothing penalties and priors are excluded. Likelihood weights need not have the same interpretation as the weights used by posterior_samples() to generate responses.

Ordinary and extended response families, distributional GAMs, multinomial, multivariate-normal and grouped families are supported. A multivariate-normal observation contributes one joint log density; its precision coefficients vary with each draw. Grouped observations use their fitted component family. Custom families can supply the log_lik hook in family_diagnostics. Quasi, censored and Cox families, residual-correlated BAMs and full mixed models are not supported. Only retained fitting observations are evaluated.

Gaussian draws approximate the coefficient posterior. Parameters represented by coefficients vary jointly, including distributional-model scale and shape predictors. Other scale, shape and smoothing parameters remain at fitted values. Even with unconditional = TRUE, those additional parameters are not jointly sampled. Ordinary PSIS-LOO uses these draws without correcting their Gaussian approximation. Pareto diagnostics assess reweighting, not the accuracy of the Gaussian approximation. See loo.gam for optional loo methods.

See also

posterior_samples(), family_diagnostics

Examples

library("mgcv")
m <- gam(mpg ~ s(wt, k = 5), data = mtcars, method = "REML")
ll <- log_lik(m, n_draws = 500, seed = 42)
dim(ll)
#> [1] 500  32
if (requireNamespace("loo", quietly = TRUE)) {
  loo::loo(ll, r_eff = 1)
}
#> 
#> Computed from 500 by 32 log-likelihood matrix.
#> 
#>          Estimate  SE
#> elpd_loo    -78.5 3.8
#> p_loo         2.9 0.8
#> looic       156.9 7.5
#> ------
#> MCSE of elpd_loo is 0.1.
#> MCSE and ESS estimates assume independent draws (r_eff=1).
#> 
#> All Pareto k estimates are good (k < 0.63).
#> See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
